newsitem.title: INDIA: New India rules for finance firms investing abroad.
newsitem.headline: New India rules for finance firms investing abroad.

text.p: India on Tuesday announced new guidelines for overseas direct investment by financial service companies, a government statement said.
It said finance companies who plan to set up joint ventures or subsidiaries abroad should have a "good track record" of a minimum of three years.
The companies must be registered with the stock market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, or with the Reserve Bank of India as a non-banking finance company, the statement said.
The government said the finance firms should have a minimum net worth of 150 million rupees and a capital adequacy ratio of 8.0 percent (of risk weighted financial assets)
"Subsidiaries of Indian financial institutions which conform to the above norms are also eligible for overseas investment," the statement said. ($1=35.8 rupees)
